# Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)

## Overview
Active substance: Paracetamol
Therapeutic area: Pain and fever
Route of administration: Oral, rectal, intravenous
Marketing authorization holder: Various
Authorization status: Authorized

## Indication
Relief of mild to moderate pain and fever reduction

## Dosage
Adults: 500-1000mg every 4-6 hours, max 4g/day

## Side Effects
- Rare allergic reactions
- Liver damage at high doses
- Skin reactions (very rare)

## Contraindications
- Severe hepatic impairment
- Known hypersensitivity to paracetamol

## Drug Interactions
- Warfarin: may enhance anticoagulant effect
- Alcohol: increased hepatotoxicity risk
- Carbamazepine: may increase hepatotoxicity risk
title: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) - Drug Information

# Ibuprofen

## Overview
Active substance: Ibuprofen
Therapeutic area: Pain and inflammation
Route of administration: Oral, topical
Marketing authorization holder: Various
Authorization status: Authorized

## Indication
Treatment of mild to moderate pain, fever, and inflammatory conditions

## Dosage
Adults: 200-400mg every 4-6 hours, max 1200mg/day (OTC) or 2400mg/day (prescription)

## Side Effects
- Gastrointestinal irritation and ulcers
- Increased cardiovascular risk with prolonged use
- Renal impairment
- Allergic reactions

## Contraindications
- History of GI bleeding or peptic ulcer
- Severe heart failure
- Third trimester of pregnancy
- Severe renal or hepatic impairment

## Drug Interactions
- Aspirin: reduced cardioprotective effect
- ACE inhibitors: reduced antihypertensive effect
- Lithium: increased lithium levels
- Methotrexate: increased toxicity
title: Ibuprofen - Drug Information

# Omeprazole

## Overview
Active substance: Omeprazole
Therapeutic area: Gastroenterology
Route of administration: Oral
Marketing authorization holder: Various (Losec by AstraZeneca)
Authorization status: Authorized

## Indication
Treatment of gastric and duodenal ulcers, GERD, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome

## Dosage
20-40mg once daily, typically before breakfast

## Side Effects
- Headache
- Nausea and diarrhea
- Vitamin B12 deficiency (long-term)
- Increased fracture risk (long-term)
- Hypomagnesemia

## Contraindications
- Known hypersensitivity to proton pump inhibitors

## Drug Interactions
- Clopidogrel: reduced antiplatelet effect
- Methotrexate: increased methotrexate levels
- Ketoconazole: reduced absorption
title: Omeprazole - Drug Information

# Amoxicillin

## Overview
Active substance: Amoxicillin
Therapeutic area: Antibiotics
Route of administration: Oral
Marketing authorization holder: Various
Authorization status: Authorized

## Indication
Bacterial infections including respiratory, urinary, and skin infections

## Dosage
Adults: 250-500mg every 8 hours or 500-875mg every 12 hours

## Side Effects
- Diarrhea
- Nausea and vomiting
- Skin rash
- Allergic reactions (including anaphylaxis)

## Contraindications
- Penicillin allergy
- History of amoxicillin-associated jaundice

## Drug Interactions
- Methotrexate: increased toxicity
- Warfarin: enhanced anticoagulant effect
- Oral contraceptives: potentially reduced efficacy
title: Amoxicillin - Drug Information

# Atorvastatin

## Overview
Active substance: Atorvastatin
Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular
Route of administration: Oral
Marketing authorization holder: Pfizer (Lipitor) and generics
Authorization status: Authorized

## Indication
Hypercholesterolemia and prevention of cardiovascular events

## Dosage
10-80mg once daily, can be taken at any time

## Side Effects
- Muscle pain and weakness (myalgia)
- Elevated liver enzymes
- Headache
- Gastrointestinal disturbances
- Rhabdomyolysis (rare)

## Contraindications
- Active liver disease
- Pregnancy and breastfeeding
- Unexplained persistent transaminase elevation

## Drug Interactions
- Cyclosporine: increased statin levels
- Gemfibrozil: increased myopathy risk
- CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, itraconazole): increased toxicity
- Grapefruit juice: increased statin levels
title: Atorvastatin - Drug Information

# Metformin

## Overview
Active substance: Metformin hydrochloride
Therapeutic area: Diabetes
Route of administration: Oral
Marketing authorization holder: Various (Glucophage by Merck)
Authorization status: Authorized

## Indication
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, particularly in overweight patients

## Dosage
Starting: 500mg once or twice daily with meals. Max: 2000-3000mg/day in divided doses

## Side Effects
- Gastrointestinal upset (nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain)
- Metallic taste
- Vitamin B12 deficiency (long-term)
- Lactic acidosis (rare but serious)

## Contraindications
- Severe renal impairment (eGFR <30)
- Acute conditions with risk of tissue hypoxia
- Diabetic ketoacidosis
- Before contrast imaging procedures

## Drug Interactions
- Alcohol: increased lactic acidosis risk
- Iodinated contrast agents: acute kidney injury risk
- ACE inhibitors: may enhance hypoglycemic effect
title: Metformin - Drug Information

# Losartan

## Overview
Active substance: Losartan potassium
Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular
Route of administration: Oral
Marketing authorization holder: MSD (Cozaar) and generics
Authorization status: Authorized

## Indication
Hypertension, heart failure, diabetic nephropathy protection

## Dosage
50mg once daily, may increase to 100mg. Take consistently with or without food

## Side Effects
- Dizziness
- Hypotension
- Hyperkalemia
- Fatigue

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy (especially 2nd and 3rd trimester)
- Bilateral renal artery stenosis
- Co-administration with aliskiren in diabetics

## Drug Interactions
- NSAIDs: reduced antihypertensive effect
- Potassium supplements: hyperkalemia risk
- Lithium: increased lithium levels
title: Losartan - Drug Information

# Salbutamol (Albuterol)

## Overview
Active substance: Salbutamol
Therapeutic area: Respiratory
Route of administration: Inhalation, oral, intravenous
Marketing authorization holder: Various (Ventolin by GSK)
Authorization status: Authorized

## Indication
Relief and prevention of bronchospasm in asthma and COPD

## Dosage
Inhalation: 100-200mcg (1-2 puffs) as needed, max 8 puffs/day

## Side Effects
- Tremor
- Tachycardia
- Headache
- Hypokalemia (with high doses)

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity to salbutamol

## Drug Interactions
- Beta-blockers: mutual antagonism
- Diuretics: enhanced hypokalemia
- MAO inhibitors: enhanced cardiovascular effects
title: Salbutamol (Albuterol) - Drug Information

# Sertraline

## Overview
Active substance: Sertraline hydrochloride
Therapeutic area: Mental health
Route of administration: Oral
Marketing authorization holder: Pfizer (Zoloft) and generics
Authorization status: Authorized

## Indication
Depression, panic disorder, OCD, PTSD, social anxiety disorder

## Dosage
Starting: 50mg/day. May increase by 50mg increments weekly. Max: 200mg/day

## Side Effects
- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Insomnia
- Sexual dysfunction
- Headache
- Serotonin syndrome (rare)

## Contraindications
- Concurrent MAO inhibitor use
- Concurrent pimozide use
- Known hypersensitivity

## Drug Interactions
- MAO inhibitors: serotonin syndrome risk (14-day washout required)
- Warfarin: increased bleeding risk
- Tramadol: seizure risk
- Alcohol: enhanced CNS depression
title: Sertraline - Drug Information

# Levothyroxine

## Overview
Active substance: Levothyroxine sodium
Therapeutic area: Endocrinology
Route of administration: Oral
Marketing authorization holder: Various
Authorization status: Authorized

## Indication
Hypothyroidism, thyroid hormone replacement

## Dosage
25-50mcg daily initially, increase every 4-6 weeks. Typical maintenance: 100-200mcg/day. Take on empty stomach

## Side Effects
- Symptoms of hyperthyroidism if overdosed (tachycardia, tremor, weight loss)
- Headache
- Insomnia
- Bone density reduction (with excess doses)

## Contraindications
- Untreated adrenal insufficiency
- Acute myocardial infarction
- Thyrotoxicosis

## Drug Interactions
- Calcium/iron supplements: reduced absorption (separate by 4 hours)
- Warfarin: enhanced anticoagulant effect
- Antacids: reduced absorption
- Carbamazepine: increased levothyroxine metabolism
title: Levothyroxine - Drug Information
